articles.author: vietnam-desk
articles.title: Vietnam Decree 342: what changes for foreign-owned retailers and distributors on 18 October 2026
articles.dek: Licences move to provincial People's Committees, the economic needs test narrows to non-treaty investors, and large store networks face a security review.
takeaways: Decree 342/2026/ND-CP, issued on 3 September 2026, takes effect on 18 October 2026 and replaces Decree 09/2018 for foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) that trade and retail goods.
The provincial People's Committee now issues the Business Licence and the Retail Outlet Licence. The economic needs test (ENT) applies only to non-treaty investors opening a second or later outlet.
A security review by the Ministries of Public Security and National Defence applies to large networks: 100+ outlets under 500 m², 50+ outlets of 500–3,000 m², or 30+ outlets of 3,000 m² or more.

head: Topic
Decree 09/2018
Decree 342/2026
rows: Provincial Department of Industry and Trade, often with prior Ministry approval
In principle, every outlet after the first
Only non-treaty investors, outlets after the first
"Scale of the geographic market", not defined
Commune or ward for outlets under 5,000 m²; province for 5,000 m² or more
Twice a year, by 15 January and 15 July
Not fixed in the same way

p: The decree also defines store formats by selling area: a convenience store is under 300 m², a mini-supermarket is up to 500 m², and a supermarket is above 500 m².

list: Japanese and Korean convenience and supermarket chains that are adding stores. Count outlets by size class: the security review starts at the thresholds above.
Buyers of local chains. After the deal is approved, the target can keep running its outlets for up to 12 months, and the Retail Outlet Licence application is due within 30 days.
Large e-commerce platforms. Foreign control of a large intermediary, social or integrated e-commerce platform also triggers the security review.

ol: Map your current and planned outlets against the three size thresholds.
If you are buying a local chain, put the 30-day licence filing into the deal timeline.
Keep existing licences: those issued before 18 October 2026 stay valid. Move to half-yearly reporting; the next report is due by 15 January 2027.

faq.q: Do existing trading licences need to be renewed under Decree 342?
faq.a: No. Business Licences and Retail Outlet Licences issued before 18 October 2026 continue to cover the activities they license.

faq.q: Does the economic needs test still apply to foreign retailers in Vietnam?
faq.a: Only to investors whose home country has no treaty commitment that removes it, and only for outlets after the first. Check the treaty that covers your home country before you file.

faq.q: What triggers the new security review?
faq.a: A non-treaty investor, foreign control of a large e-commerce platform, or a network of at least 100 outlets under 500 m², 50 outlets of 500–3,000 m², or 30 outlets of 3,000 m² or more.

articles.author: indonesia-desk
articles.title: Indonesia's halal deadline for imported food and drinks: what importers need by 17 October 2026
articles.dek: Imported food and beverages must hold a recognised halal certificate before they reach shelves. Customs clearance is not blocked.
takeaways: Under Government Regulation 42/2024 (Article 160(3)), halal certification for imported food, beverages, slaughtered products and slaughtering services applies no later than 17 October 2026. The halal agency BPJPH says enforcement starts on 18 October.
It is not an import ban. Goods can clear customs, but they must meet halal rules before they are distributed to retail or food service, according to Trade Minister Budi Santoso.

There are two routes: full Indonesian certification through a halal inspection body (LPH), or registration with BPJPH of a certificate from a foreign halal body that has a mutual recognition agreement with BPJPH.

head: Product
What applies
rows: Halal certificate required before distribution, from 17 October 2026
Inherently non-halal products (for example pork, alcohol)
No certificate, but a clear non-halal statement on the label
Products not compliant after the deadline
Written warning, then fines, then certificate revocation and product recall

p: BPJPH issued Regulation No. 4 of 2026 on 5 September 2026 to set out how foreign products are checked. In a 2023 survey cited by consultants, 83% of Indonesian consumers called the halal logo a main purchase factor, rising to 93% for food and drinks.

ol: Check that your halal certifier is on BPJPH's list of recognised foreign halal bodies. If it is not, start Indonesian certification through an LPH.
Register your foreign certificate with BPJPH before goods leave the importer's warehouse.
Relabel non-halal lines with a clear non-halal statement.
Expect distributors and modern retail buyers to ask for proof of halal status at listing.

faq.q: Will imported food without a halal certificate be stopped at the port?
faq.a: No. The Trade Minister has said halal certification is not an import restriction. Goods can clear customs, but they cannot be distributed in Indonesia until halal requirements are met.

faq.q: Is a halal certificate from my home country accepted in Indonesia?
faq.a: Only if the issuing body has a mutual recognition agreement with BPJPH and the certificate is registered with BPJPH. Otherwise the product needs Indonesian certification.

faq.q: Do pork or alcoholic products need halal certification?
faq.a: No. Inherently non-halal products need a clear non-halal statement on the label instead, and still follow normal food safety and labelling rules.

articles.author: thailand-desk
articles.title: Thailand's data centre pause: what the 166 halted projects mean for investors
articles.dek: Thailand froze 49 builds and 117 approvals on 4 September while it writes national rules. Size classes were approved on 1 October, and the full criteria go to Cabinet next.
takeaways: On 4 September 2026, the first meeting of the Data Center Business Policy Committee halted 49 projects under construction and put 117 approvals on hold, 166 in total. Sources differ on whether the halt is binding or a request to cooperate.

On 1 October 2026, the committee approved a separate legal definition for data centre buildings, with five size classes based on power use. They set rules on safety, structure, water reserves and backup fuel. Operators that have already built get a transition period.

The draft framework would treat data centres above 2 MW as industrial operations (a possible factory licence and environmental impact assessment), screen projects centrally, and give a lower power rate to operators buying renewable power through direct PPAs.

p: Approvals ran ahead of the rules. The BOI promoted 42 data centre projects worth about THB 750 billion from 2024 to 2026. Thailand had about 216 MW of capacity in operation and 944 MW under construction or planned in Q2 2026. Information sat with 16 agencies, and there is no single data centre law.

head: Group
What changes
rows: Paused; a transition period is planned for those that do not meet the new criteria
On hold until the national criteria are published
In-house data centres of manufacturers and banks
The draft covers them too, not only colocation providers
A lower electricity rate is proposed

ol: Add schedule buffers to Thai projects until the criteria and transition rules are published.
Check whether an in-house facility above 2 MW would fall under factory licensing.
Line up renewable supply through a direct PPA, since the proposed rate design favours it.

faq.q: Is Thailand closing to data centre investment?
faq.a: No. The draft framework still prioritises digital, AI and cloud businesses and keeps tax incentives. The pause is about setting common standards for power, water, sites and safety.

faq.q: When will Thailand's data centre rules be final?
faq.a: After the 1 October meeting, the subcommittees aimed to finish the criteria within days, and then go to the committee and the Cabinet. The government said all steps should be completed within about a month.

faq.q: Do the rules apply to a company's own server rooms?
faq.a: The draft framework covers captive and in-house facilities as well as commercial providers, and proposes industrial classification above 2 MW.

articles.author: malaysia-desk
articles.title: Malaysia Budget 2027: the tax changes that matter for foreign investors
articles.dek: Tabled on 9 October 2026: a 5% rate for regional hubs for up to 30 years, longer allowances for local machinery and green investment, and a higher minimum wage.
takeaways: The Global Services Hub incentive offers a 5% special corporate tax rate for qualifying regional headquarters, shared services and treasury activities, for up to 30 years, from 1 January 2027.
The accelerated capital allowance for locally purchased plant, machinery and ICT equipment is extended to 31 December 2030. So is the Green Investment Tax Allowance of up to 100%.
The minimum wage rises from RM1,700 to RM2,000 in June 2027 (+18%). Small and medium firms with sales under RM50 million are exempt.

head: Measure
Detail
Who it affects
rows: 15% to 14% on the first RM150,000; 17% to 16% up to RM600,000
SMEs, saving up to RM6,000 a year
5% for up to 30 years, from 1 January 2027
Regional HQs, shared services, treasury centres
Capital allowance, local machinery and ICT
Allowed only for wages paid through permitted bank channels

p: Federal spending rises 3.6% to RM459.8 billion, and the deficit target falls from 3.6% to 3.3% of GDP. Approved investments reached RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026. These are budget proposals and still need to pass Parliament.

list: For companies choosing a regional base, the 5% hub rate for up to 30 years is the headline offer.
Manufacturers keep the faster allowance only on equipment bought locally, which favours local suppliers.
Labour costs rise by 18% at the minimum wage level from mid-2027 for firms above the RM50 million threshold.

faq.q: When does Malaysia's Global Services Hub 5% rate start?
faq.a: From 1 January 2027, for qualifying regional headquarters, shared services and treasury activities, with incentive periods of up to 30 years.

faq.q: Who pays the new RM2,000 minimum wage?
faq.a: All employers from June 2027, except micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million.

faq.q: Are the Budget 2027 tax changes already law?
faq.a: Not yet. They were tabled on 9 October 2026 and take effect once Parliament passes the Finance Bill, so details can change.

articles.author: philippines-desk
articles.title: Philippine power prices rose again in October: what it means for manufacturers and data centres
articles.dek: Meralco's generation charge rose ₱0.4973 per kWh, driven by LNG-linked supply and a weak peso. The typical household rate is now ₱15.0615 per kWh.
takeaways: In October 2026, Meralco's rate for a typical household rose ₱0.3191 to ₱15.0615 per kWh. The generation charge, which business customers also pay, rose ₱0.4973 per kWh.
The cause is supply from First Gas and Prime CoreGen (about 24% of the mix), up ₱3.2206 per kWh on high LNG prices. About 89% of its costs are in US dollars, so the weak peso adds to it.
The Department of Energy said in July that the Philippines' average power price (₱12.43 per kWh in June) was the highest in Southeast Asia, ₱0.09 above Singapore.

p: Meralco serves more than 8.3 million customers. A ₱2.64 billion refund, about ₱0.1020 per kWh on average across customer classes, starts with the November 2026 bill and runs for six months.

list: Energy-intensive factories on the Luzon grid, such as electronics assembly and cold chain.
Data centres and large office sites, where power is a main operating cost.
Companies with peso revenue and dollar-linked energy costs.

ol: Budget power at current LNG-linked levels, not at the lower rates of earlier years.
Compare grid supply with on-site solar or a renewable supply contract.
Treat the peso exchange rate as a power cost driver in site comparisons.

faq.q: Why did Philippine electricity rates rise in October 2026?
faq.a: Mainly a higher generation charge: gas-fired supply from First Gas and Prime CoreGen cost more because LNG prices stayed high and the peso was weak, and spot market prices rose on tight Luzon supply.

faq.q: Are Meralco customers getting a refund?
faq.a: Yes. A ₱2.64 billion refund starts with the November 2026 billing cycle and runs over six months, averaging about ₱0.1020 per kWh across customer classes.

faq.q: Is Philippine electricity the most expensive in Southeast Asia?
faq.a: The Department of Energy said in July 2026 that the June average of ₱12.43 per kWh was the highest in the region, slightly above Singapore.
